{{Quote|The Sith Empire will burn brightly, like a supernova, dwarfing the complacent Republic. We shall hold the entire galaxy in our grasp.|Naga Sadow|<ref name="fotse1" />}}
'''Naga Sadow''' was a master [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemist]] and [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] who, in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], took the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] to the brink of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] domination in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. A [[Hybrid/Legends|half-breed]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] from [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], Sadow was [[Sith training|trained]] by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Simus]] and ruled over a [[Naga Sadow's Khar Shian citadel|secret citadel]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Khar Shian]], where [[Gender/Legends|he]] became one of the most powerful [[Sith sorcerer|Sith sorcerers]] of his [[Time/Legends|time]]. A member of the [[Sith Council]] under the reign of Dark Lord of the Sith [[Marka Ragnos]], Sadow's preached an expansionist philosophy that put him at odds with much of the isolated Sith Empire's establishment. Sadow was considered a major candidate for Dark Lord after Ragnos' [[Death/Legends|death]], leading him into a power struggle with conservative rival [[Ludo Kressh]] that only ended with the surprise arrival of two [[Scout/Legends|explorers]] from the far-off [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]].

Sadow saw opportunity in the two explorers&mdash;siblings [[Gav Daragon|Gav]] and [[Jori Daragon]], and used the suspicion and fear raised by their arrival to foment war with the Republic. Along the way, Sadow [[Battle of Khar Delba|shattered]] [[Ludo Kressh's faction|Kressh's forces]] at [[Khar Delba]], leaving no challengers to his authority. With Kressh seemingly out of the picture, Sadow gathered together all the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] and built a formidable military force to conquer the Republic, while also taking Gav Daragon as his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]]. When the time was right, Sadow and his forces launched a massive surprise attack on the Republic, a many-pronged strike aimed at conquering the important [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]] while seizing the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. For his part, Sadow stayed isolated in his [[Sith Meditation Sphere|Sith meditation sphere]], augmenting his forces with [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusion|illusory]] beasts and [[Starship/Legends|ships]].

Sadow's efforts initially met with great success, and he was on the cusp of victory when events turned against him. Gav Daragon turned coat once back [[Cinnagar/Legends|home]] and attacked Sadow in his meditation sphere, breaking his concentration and dissipating his illusions. His momentum halted, Sadow killed Daragon and fled home, only to find a still-alive Ludo Kressh waiting for him with his own [[Army/Legends|army]]. Sadow managed to deal his rival a [[First battle of Korriban|final defeat]] before immediately being forced into [[Second battle of Korriban|battle]] again with a pursuing Republic force. Seeing he could not win, Sadow escaped with a daring [[Battle at the Denarii Nova|run]] through the twin [[Star/Legends|stars]] of the [[Denarii Nova]], destroying both stars along with his pursuers, and made his way to the uninhabited moon of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Sadow practiced his [[Sith sorcery/Legends|alchemy]] alone there for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]], building massive temple complexes, before voluntarily placing himself in [[Suspended animation/Legends|suspended animation]].

He was awoken some [[4400 BBY|600 years later]] by a fallen [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] named [[Freedon Nadd]], who learned the former Dark Lord of the Sith's secrets before killing him. Sadow was [[Naga Sadow's tomb|entombed]] by his Massassi servants on Yavin 4, and the Sith Lord's legacy and lost artifacts continued to draw the interests of other Sith and archaeologists long after his death.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Simus was my mentor, my teacher&hellip; the noblest among us&hellip; he always offered his wisdom.|Naga Sadow on his mentor, Simus|<ref name="gaots3" />}}
[[File:SternNaga.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Naga Sadow]]
Naga Sadow was born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] in the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], a rich but isolated civilization<ref name="negtc" /> concealed from the [[The galaxy/Legends|greater galaxy]] by the difficult-to-navigate [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] known as the [[Stygian Caldera]],<ref name="paragon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> centuries before [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]].<ref name="negtcdate" /> Around [[7000 BBY|two thousand years]] before Sadow's lifetime, the [[Second Great Schism]] led to a [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|century-long war]] between [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], with a [[Exiles|cadre of]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Battle of Corbos|defeated]] and exiled.<ref name="jvs">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> They went on to [[Discovery of Korriban|discover]], conquer and interbreed with the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]], becoming the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] and establishing their "lost" empire. Sadow was an heir to this legacy,<ref name="negtc" /> being a Sith [[Blood/Legends|Pureblood]]&mdash;a hybrid of the Sith and their [[Human/Legends|Human]] Dark Jedi conquerers.<ref name="TORE" /> While Sadow had Sith features, including [[Color/Legends|red]] skin and tendrils on his face,<ref name="gaots2" /> the hybrid also boasted a strong bloodline<ref name="gaots3" />&mdash;one of the purest Jedi lineages in the Sith Empire.<ref name="negtc" />

Despite the empire's splendor in the so-called [[Golden Age of the Sith]],<ref name="gaots2" /> Sadow grew up in an age where the Sith civilization faced many crises. Being so far removed from the rest of the galaxy stagnated the Sith Empire's economic growth and technological knowledge, while the old aristocracy had died off to be replaced by half-caste warriors consumed with quests for power. Meanwhile, the specter of the Jedi and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] hung over Sith society like a boogeyman, with fearful rumors constantly circulating that the Republic was planning the overthrow of the Sith Empire. Sadow was raised from birth to fight these threats<ref name="warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and eventually came under the tutelage of the Sith Lord [[Simus]], who served as both a teacher and a mentor to Sadow. Simus would serve as a guiding figure throughout Sadow's life, even after he was beheaded in a duel with [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Marka Ragnos]], as he used his Sith powers to keep his head alive in a crystalline jar. By [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="gaots3" /> Sadow had used the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] to extend his life for centuries<ref name="negtcdate" /> and had grown in stature among the Sith Lords, becoming a member of the ten-member [[Sith Council]], serving alongside his mentor Simus.<ref name="gaots3" />

As was the custom of Sith Lords at the time, Sadow set about building his own personal army, but typically unorthodox as he was, Sadow absorbed outside cultures into his service instead of drawing his forces exclusively from his [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] population.<ref name="errant">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']]</ref> Sadow soon became well-known among the Sith Lords of his time, and preached an expansionist philosophy for a number of years.<ref name="deceptionscodex">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 26: Naga Sadow's Deceptions}}</ref> While Sadow was nominally in control of the world of [[Khar Delba]], the world was just a decoy&mdash;<ref name="gaots4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> Sadow's true work occurred on a secret stronghold on the dark side of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Khar Shian]], where he found it better to further his research into the dark arts.<ref name="gaots3" /> Among the dark side pursuits that Sadow embarked on during this time was a fruitless search for the [[Muur Talisman]]&mdash;an ancient [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulet]] with the power to turn people into monstrous [[rakghoul]]s. Sadow competed with a number of other Sith Lords of the time to find the Talisman first.<ref name="kotor25">[[Knights of the Old Republic 25|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 25]]</ref> As part of this pursuit, Sadow translated the [[Codex of Karness Muur|Codex]] of the long-dead Sith Lord [[Karness Muur]], creator of the Talisman.<ref name="kotor28">[[Knights of the Old Republic 28|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 28]]</ref>

===Claimant to the Sith legacy===
{{Quote|Unlike Ludo Kressh, I refuse to cower in the shadows at this threat. I refuse to tremble like a coward and wait for the enemy to come after us. ''We must fight back!'' We must unite! We must prepare! In such troubled times, we do not dare allow ourselves to be without a leader. Marka Ragnos is dead, and we must choose a new Dark Lord. And it must be me.|Naga Sadow|<ref name="gaots3" />}}
[[File:LudoVsSadow.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Naga Sadow battles Ludo Kressh at Dark Lord Marka Ragnos' funeral.]]
Towards the end of Marka Ragnos' [[Standard century/Legends|century]]-long reign as Dark Lord of the Sith, Sadow had begun to covet the position for himself. Sadow had grown to resent what he saw as the Sith's stagnation, as they wallowed endlessly in their riches. Sadow believed it was time for a change, and when Ragnos passed away in 5000 BBY, he would have his chance. Ragnos' [[Death/Legends|death]] was immediately followed by a grand [[Funeral of Marka Ragnos|funeral procession]] through [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban's]] [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]], led by Sadow's greatest rival for the throne of Dark Lord, [[Ludo Kressh]]. Sadow arrived late, as Ragnos' [[Sith sarcophagus|sarcophagus]] was already on its way to its [[Tomb of Marka Ragnos|tomb]], and when the tardy Sadow ascended the steps of Ragnos' newly-built tomb to take his place in the ceremony, Kressh ordered him to turn back, saying that he was shaming Ragnos' memory. An indignant Sadow stepped up to state his claim for the title of Dark Lord of the Sith, something which was immediately opposed by the much more conservative Kressh&mdash;in accordance with the Sith traditions, the only logical way to resolve this impasse was for Sadow and Kressh to do battle. Facing off on the threshold of Ragnos' tomb, the two Sith Lords dueled with [[Force-imbued sword/Legends|Force-imbued blades]], as it quickly became apparent that this would be a fight to the death.<ref name="gaots2" />

Neither would get the chance to claim a victory, however, as Marka Ragnos' [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] appeared with a warning: the Golden Age was nearing its end, and the Sith would need to fight the correct battles or else be destroyed. As the Sadow and Kressh pondered the dead Dark Lord's words, they were interrupted by an unexpected sight: a [[Starbreaker 12|starship]] of unknown origin descending into the Valley of the Dark Lords. When the ship landed, two Humans disembarked, proclaiming themselves to be emissaries from the Galactic Republic interested in setting up a trade relationship with the Sith civilization. The pair&mdash;[[Gav Daragon|Gav]] and [[Jori Daragon]], in truth fugitives who had chanced upon Korriban after making a blind [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump to escape trouble on their native [[Empress Teta/Legends|Koros Major]]&mdash;were swiftly seized as [[Spy/Legends|spies]]. Although Kressh wanted to kill them immediately, Sadow thought the Daragons could be the key to new Sith conquests,<ref name="gaots2" /> and they were imprisoned for questioning on Ziost.<ref name="gaots3" />

For Sadow, the Republic was a vast new field to conquer, but it could also be a unifying force for an increasingly split Sith Empire, and a distraction from political weaknesses on the homefront.<ref name="tec">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> With the Daragons in chains, Sadow met with the rest of the Sith Council at Ziost's [[Sith Citadel (Ziost)|Sith Citadel]] to discuss their fates. While several of the Council agreed with Kressh that the visitors should be put to death, Sadow made an impassioned plea to keep them alive, as their knowledge of the rest of the galaxy could lead to greater Sith domination and control.<ref name="gaots3" /> Sadow knew well the value that Humans could bring, as he had made good use of the scientific skills of the descendants of Human [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani]] refugees that had been enslaved by the Sith generations before, and often included Humans among his entourage.<ref name="paragon" />

[[File:Naga_Sadow_blasting.jpg|thumb|left|224px|Sadow and his followers raided Ziost, leaving no evidence but a Republic blaster.]]
Despite Sadow's plea, the Council still voted to kill the Daragons. However, the ever-ambitious Sadow still had the galaxy on his mind, and he put a plan in motion to rescue the explorers and bring the rest of the Sith Council around to his side. As Sadow watched from his secret fortress on Khar Shian, a Sith soldier loyal to Sadow snuck into the Daragons' ship and stole a pair of Republic [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]]. Once the weapons were in hand, Sadow quickly raided Ziost with a small strike team, freeing the Daragons and killing all witnesses using one of the Republic blasters, including his old teacher, Simus. Sadow left the weapon behind at the scene, and departed to allow the rest of the Sith Lords to draw their own conclusions. Sadow deposited the Daragons at his secret citadel on Khar Shian, before promptly returning to Ziost to see if his strike had had the effect he desired. Sadow arrived to find that everything had gone according to plan: the Sith Council was in a panic, and the Republic was to blame. Feigning shock at Simus' death, Sadow loudly proclaimed that it was time for the Sith to strike back, and officially announced his intentions to seize the title of Dark Lord. To Ludo Kressh's horror, several of the Sith Council backed Sadow's claim, and Kressh left in a huff with his supporters, proclaiming that he would become the true Dark Lord. Not willing to let this stand, Sadow ordered his supporters, each of whom controlled a dozen worlds, to call their ships and warriors to battle. Things had come to a head, and Naga Sadow and Ludo Kressh were finally going to war.<ref name="gaots3" />

===Consolidating power===
{{Quote|Your spies have failed you. ''Everything'' has failed you, Ludo. You never should have imagined your petty scheme could surpass my grand dreams&hellip; as you shall see&hellip;|Naga Sadow, as the tide turns at Khar Delba|<ref name="gaots5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 5]]</ref>}}
[[File:SadowRalliesTheTroops.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Naga Sadow rallies Sith forces after the Battle of Khar Delba.]]
In the meantime, Sadow split the Daragons up, keeping Gav Daragon with him on Khar Shian and sending his sister Jori to his decoy fortress on Khar Delba. In Gav Daragon, who had once been a low-level initiate of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in his younger days, he found someone with a strong, if untrained, talent in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Sensing promise in Daragon, Sadow took him under his wing as an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] and began to teach the young man [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]]. With all-out war with Ludo Kressh looming, Sadow had a traditional [[mark of Dark Lord of the Sith]] applied to his forehead by [[Sith pincerbug]]s, an act which most believed made his claim to the seat of Dark Lord official. Soon afterward, he received information that Ludo Kressh had his men guarding the Daragons' captured ship, the ''Starbreaker 12''.<ref name="gaots4" />

Realizing an opportunity, Sadow sent several of his [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors to kill Kressh's guards and seize the ship, leaving no witnesses and leaving Sadow's emblem behind at the scene. Sadow's Massassi flew the ''Starbreaker 12'' back to Khar Delba, getting there just before Kressh [[Battle of Khar Delba|attacked]] the world, just as Sadow had foreseen. Having planned for this eventuality, Sadow allowed Kressh, backed by the forces of his allies [[Horak-mul]] and [[Dor Gal-ram]], to batter his fortresses on Khar Delba with a rain of [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire from their [[Derriphan-class battleship|battleships]].<ref name="gaots4" /> Although completely unconcerned about Kressh's firepower, Sadow feigned panic, quickly ushering Jori Daragon to the recovered ''Starbreaker 12'', claiming he was protecting her from [[Torture/Legends|torture]] and death at Kressh's hands. In fact, Sadow simply wanted her to escape alone, so he could follow her [[Daragon Trail|trail]] back to the unsuspecting Republic, while keeping her brother Gav with him as his apprentice.<ref name="gaots5" />

Jori Daragon, who did not believe she had any reason not to trust Naga Sadow, completely fell for the Sith Lord's feigned concern and followed his instructions to escape back to her home&mdash;unbeknownst to her, Sadow had outfitted her ship with a [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]]. While Kressh's bombardment continued, Daragon managed to evade the laserfire in the ''Starbreaker 12'' and jump to hyperspace. Once Daragon was clear of the battlefield, Sadow put the second part of his plan into motion, calling his [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] from its hiding place on the dark side of Khar Shian. The fleet's arrival and sudden attack took Kressh completely by surprise, as another level of subterfuge tore Kressh's ranks apart:<ref name="gaots5" /> several of Sadow's [[Sadow'een]] assassins,<ref name="horakmul">{{TORcite|type=|Conversation with Horak-mul}}</ref> posing as crewmembers on Kressh's battleships, attacked and killed Horak-mul and Dor Gal-ram and commandeered their vessels. Withering laserfire from both within and without forced Kressh into an ignominious retreat. Sadow's tactical masterpiece at Khar Delba cemented him as the undisputed ruler of the Sith Empire, while Daragon's escape back to the Republic had set the stage for a Sith invasion of the rest of the galaxy at large. His fleet and power only growing, Sadow knew the time was coming to strike, and he rallied all the rest of the Sith Lords to join his impending conquest of the Galactic Republic.<ref name="gaots5" />

[[File:Dark_Lord_Naga_Sadow-Timeline12.jpg|thumb|250px|Naga Sadow, Dark Lord of the Sith]]
With Ludo Kressh out of the picture, Naga Sadow began furiously preparing for his attack on the Republic, working his Massassi workers' fingers to the bone repairing the damage done to his citadel on Khar Delba and raising his fleet.<ref name="fotse1" /> Now the undisputed Dark Lord of the Sith, Naga Sadow was pledged the allegiance of all the rest of the Sith Lords and their armies.<ref name="warfare" /> Sadow also kept himself busy grooming Gav Daragon&mdash;who was becoming increasingly morally conflicted at the prospect of attacking his home in the Republic&mdash;as his dark apprentice, although he often found himself having to lie to keep the young Human in the fold. While his war fleet was being fully readied, Sadow gathered the other Sith Lords to a war council on Khar Delba, which was interrupted by an unexpected arrival: Ludo Kressh, who broadcast an anti-Sadow transmission to the Sith Lords at the same time that his [[Ludo Kressh's flagship|flagship]] was spotted approaching Khar Delba. Dismissive of Kressh's "prattle," Sadow ordered Daragon to press a button on a nearby control panel, promising it would block Kressh's transmission. When Daragon pressed the button, however, Kressh's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] violently exploded, and the obstacle that was Ludo Kressh was seemingly gone for good. Daragon was stunned, even more so when Sadow revealed that they had the location of their Republic target due to a tracer he had placed on the ''Starbreaker 12''. Sadow had no time to argue with his young apprentice, however&mdash;before the explosion in Khar Delba's atmosphere had even subsided, he proclaimed the time had come to launch his attack.<ref name="fotse1" />

===Sadow's star war===
{{Quote|We have a war to commence! Fleet commanders, you have your orders! Strike swiftly and decisively to consume Teta's worlds&hellip; others will stab the heart of the Republic. We can dominate Coruscant in an eyeblink!|Naga Sadow|<ref name="fotse3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:NagaSadowInMothership-TFotSE4.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Naga Sadow conjures illusions in his meditation sphere during the Great Hyperspace War.]]
Sadow was able to put together an extremely formidable fighting force with remarkable quickness, as ships, ground troops and war beasts flocked to him from every corner of the Sith worlds. Once the moment of truth came, Sadow gathered his invasion fleet at Khar Shian. His plan was set: the Dark Lord would lead the war effort from his [[Naga Sadow's Mothership|Sith meditation sphere]], which would be the heart and mind of the Sith attack. To give his forces a psychological edge, Sadow planned to keep to his [[Sith Meditation Sphere|meditation sphere]], using Sith magic to create [[Mind trick/Legends#Force illusions|illusions]] that would make his forces appear much more formidable than they were.<ref name="fotse2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 2]]</ref>

Over objections from Gav Daragon, Sadow intended to leave Sith Space undefended and toss his entire strength at the Republic. Furthermore, Sadow placed Daragon, who had no command experience, in charge of one of his flagships. Once everything was set, Sadow called for his fleet to launch to hyperspace, proclaiming that the Republic would be theirs.<ref name="fotse2" /> Locking onto the beacon from the ''Starbreaker 12'', the Sith fleet soon arrived at the ship's location within Republic space. Sensing no Humans aboard&mdash;the ship had recently been taken from Jori Daragon by a creditor, [[Ssk Kahorr]]&mdash;Sadow ordered the ship's destruction, and next dispatched his fleet as according to his war plan. Gav Daragon and the main fleet would strike quickly to consume the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]], while another part of his forces would strike at the very heart of the Republic.<ref name="fotse3" />

As his fleet departed, Sadow retired in his meditation sphere<ref name="fotse3" /> to the [[Primus Goluud system]],<ref name="fotse4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref> where he began working on conjuring his illusions. In a bold move, Sith forces began the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|war]] with a [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Hyperspace War)|direct attack]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] itself, the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the Republic, part of a many-pronged Sith assault. Led by Sith Lord [[Shar Dakhan]], the Sith invasion force on Coruscant was bolstered with Sadow's illusions to make it appear tens of thousands of ships strong, while Daragon's group [[Battle of Koros Major (Great Hyperspace War)|laid siege]] to the Koros system against a combined army of [[Tetan/Legends|Tetan]] military and pardoned [[Kirrek]] rebels.<ref name="fotse3" />

In the run-up to his attempt to take Kirrek, Sadow sent [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] fallen Jedi [[Saes Rrogon]] to seek out rare [[Lignan crystal]]s, which had the ability to bolster a dark side user's Force power. Sadow delayed his attack until Rrogon found a significant deposit on [[Phaegon III]],<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> and with [[Battle of Kirrek (Great Hyperspace War)|combat already raging]] on Kirrek, Sadow personally dispatched one of his most trusted [[Captain/Legends|captains]], [[Yaru Korsin]], to mine those crystals. However, both Korsin's ''[[Omen]]'' and sister ship [[Harbinger (Sith dreadnaught)|''Harbinger'']] were lost to a [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|Jedi attack]].<ref name="precipice">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref> Sadow's campaigns in this sector of the galaxy initially met with great success, as Sadow's spotty knowledge of the region actually worked in his favor, granting his forces a degree of unpredictability.<ref name="nec" /> But while he seemed on the verge of victory, at a critical moment came a circumstance Sadow had not planned for. After encountering his sister Jori in the burning streets of his home [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Cinnagar/Legends|Cinnagar]], Gav Daragon had a change of heart and fled the battle in his warship, tracking Sadow to the [[Primus Goluud/Legends|Primus Goluud]] system.<ref name="fotse4" />

After finding Sadow's meditation sphere, Daragon blasted it with a powerful laser shot, breaking Sadow's concentration and forcing many of his apparitions to disappear across the galaxy. On Coruscant, an outnumbered contingent of Jedi and Republic [[Republic Military/Legends|soldiers]] had been backed up to the steps of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and the confusion led to a Republic counterstrike that ultimately defeated the Sith. His vessel damaged but not destroyed, Sadow sent a transmission to Daragon, asking him to come to his listing sphere so they could meet face to face. Daragon obliged only to realize he had been tricked, as a furious Sadow had abandoned the ship and trapped him there, promising to deal with him later. By then, a Sith victory seemed a much more unlikely proposition, a hope dimmed even further after reinforcements from [[Ronika/Legends|Ronika]] overcame the Sith forces on Kirrek.<ref name="fotse4" />

Sadow's grab for the Republic was falling apart, and as [[Empress/Legends|Empress]] [[Teta/Legends|Teta's]] forces reaffirmed their claim to the Koros system, the Empress herself, along with Jori Daragon, followed Gav's hyperspace trail to Primus Goluud. Sadow recalled the battered remnants of his fleet, and immediately [[Battle at Primus Goluud|attacked]] when the enemy ships arrived. Sadow was outgunned, but he had an ace in the hole: the power of Sith magic. Within the [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] [[Corsair (Derriphan-class)|''Corsair'']], Sadow used the Force to [[Supernova (Sith magic)|trigger]] a massive [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] in the [[Star/Legends|star]] Primus Goluud, covering his retreat and consuming Gav Daragon, still trapped in the meditation sphere. But in Daragon's last moments, he had given his sister a critical piece of intelligence: Sadow had left the Sith Worlds abandoned to attack the Republic, and Empress Teta had a chance to put an end to the Sith Empire in one fell swoop.<ref name="fotse4" />

===Flight, exile and death===
{{Quote|So this is how it ends&hellip; I must run and hide! I, Naga Sadow&ndash;I, who was Dark Lord of the Sith!|Naga Sadow|<ref name="fotse5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]]</ref>}}
With the Sith invasion shattered at Coruscant, Koros Major and Primus Goluud, only a few ships remained to limp back to Sith Space with Sadow. His assault on the Republic had been decisively repelled, but Sadow did not believe the war was over and planned on licking his wounds, raising new forces and preparing for a second go-around. However, Sadow had an unexpected welcoming party once he returned home: Ludo Kressh, who had staged his own death at Khar Delba, gathered his own forces and proclaimed himself Dark Lord of the Sith in Sadow's absence. With little time to recover after Primus Goluud, Sadow found himself engaged in [[First battle of Korriban|another battle]], this against his oldest rival in the skies above Korriban. Kressh nearly overwhelmed Sadow's battered ships, but one of Sadow's doomed [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] made a suicide run on Kressh's flagship, killing the would-be Dark Lord and breaking his remaining forces' will to fight. To his shock, yet another fleet soon emerged from hyperspace: Empress Teta and her ships from the Koros system, which had followed his trail from Primus Goluud. Sadow vowed to [[Second battle of Korriban|fight to the death]], but he and his fleet had nothing left. Once his defeat was apparent, and Empress Teta demanded his surrender, Sadow realized that he only had one chance to emerge alive. Sadow had his few remaining ships assemble a blockade, while he made a run for the twin stars of the [[Denarii Nova]].<ref name="fotse5" />

[[File:Nagasadowyavin4.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Naga Sadow arrives in exile on Yavin 4.]]
As Sadow's ''Corsair'' made the treacherous journey between the Denarii Nova's [[Binary star system/Legends|binary stars]], pursued by Tetan forces, Sadow&mdash;much like he did at Primus Goluud&mdash;[[Battle at the Denarii Nova|used]] Sith magic to cause [[Solar flare/Legends|solar flares]] and cover his retreat. As she watched the destruction of Sadow's blockade and her ships in pursuit of the Sith Lord, Empress Teta mistakenly believed that Sadow had to have been killed, and ordered her fleet back to Republic space. But Sadow had escaped in the ''Corsair'', the last ship remaining in his mighty Sith invasion fleet. Sadow eventually stumbled across the uninhabited, uncharted [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]], containing the lush moon [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], where Sadow decided to make a new start. Sadow quickly set his remaining Massassi to work, taming the jungle<ref name="fotse5" /> and raising a series of [[Massassi Temple (disambiguation)|massive temples]].<ref name="dlots4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> Sadow used the [[Temple of Fire]] to conceal his ''Corsair'', the only ship that could have taken him off the jungle moon.<ref name="dlots5">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 5]]</ref> At some point, a [[statue of Naga Sadow]] was erected in the temple.<ref name="EGtC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

On Yavin 4, Sadow continued his studies of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]], learning how to assert his will on the natural order of the universe. His Sith Empire unmade, Sadow instead set his sights on creating a race of warriors powerful enough to protect what remained of his legacy. To this end he experimented upon his Massassi slaves, twisting and mutating them into powerful beings filled with violence and hate. At some point, Sadow became aware of a [[Dark Lord prophecy|prophecy]] that foretold the return of the Dark Lords of the Sith.<ref name="dlots4" /> Sadow experimented on other creatures, including a larval [[Exogorth/Legends|space slug]] that had attached itself to the ''Corsair'' en route to Yavin 4. Not seeing any use for the beast after several unsuccessful attempts to tame it, Sadow decided to mutate it into a giant monster that could swallow a Jedi in one bite: the colossal [[Sith wyrm]], which continued to live deep under Sadow's temples for centuries<ref name="dss">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> as a guardian against the future Dark Lord.<ref name="dlots4" /> However, Sadow soon faced a challenge from a tribe of intelligent, cultured and independent Massassi that had managed to escape his experiments. Resenting Sadow's uncontested rule, the Massassi tribe struck at Sadow's temples, and even though the Dark Lord had anticipated their aggression, the Massassi tribe fought through Sadow's twisted warriors and forced a face-to-face confrontation. As Sadow commended the Massassi tribesmen for their bravery, hundreds of Sadow's brutes flooded the chamber and took the attackers captive, for Sadow to subject them to the same alchemical processes that turned their brothers into mindless beasts.<ref name="massassicodex">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Massassi War}}</ref>

After decades practicing his Sith alchemy undisturbed,<ref name="dss" /> Sadow decided that it was time to place himself in a suspended animation chamber that would keep his body alive for centuries,<ref name="nec" /> making a vow not to return until the fires of conflict had burned out<ref name="tec" /> and a new apprentice had risen to bring about a Sith golden age.<ref name="nec" /> That day came around [[4400 BBY]], when he was discovered and awakened by a curious Jedi named [[Freedon Nadd]], who had stumbled upon Yavin 4 during his quest to learn more of the dark side.<ref name="negtc" /> Believing that Nadd was the apprentice for whom he had been waiting for centuries,<ref name="naddcodex" /> Sadow taught Nadd his Sith secrets,<ref name="negtc" /> only for his newfound apprentice to eventually turn on and kill him.<ref name="naddcodex" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Ask me of my heritage, and I shall tell you. Ask me of my ambitions, and you shall know them. Ask me for my hand in battle, and I shall likely lend you both. But ask me the secrets of Sith alchemy, and I would ask you for three measures of blood: one from a person you love, one from a person you hate, and one from yourself.|Naga Sadow, recorded on a holocron found long after his death|<ref name="jvs" />}}
[[File:Tfotse12.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Naga Sadow constructing the temples on Yavin 4 that would outlive him by millennia.]]
Sadow's attack on the Republic, and his daring escape from pursuit at Korriban, would in turn inspire subsequent generations of Sith,<ref name="dlots1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> including future Dark Lord of the Sith<ref name="nec" /> [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], who learned Sadow's tale from [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]]' [[Tedryn Holocron|holocron]] while still a Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]].<ref name="dlots1" /> Guided by the spirit of Freedon Nadd&mdash;who had become a powerful Sith Lord himself&mdash; and fascinated by forbidden dark side knowledge, Kun followed Sadow's trail<ref name="dlots3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> to Yavin 4, finding his ancient temples and the descendants of his Massassi slaves, who had devolved into mutated primitives.<ref name="dlots4" />

The Massassi captured Kun and sentenced him to die, and summoned the massive Sith wyrm left over from Sadow's experiments to test his power. As he struggled in the beast's grasp, Kun heard Nadd's call who urged him to use the dark side and revealed to him that Sadow feared the prophecy of the Dark Lords and created the wyrm to destroy Kun. Through an exertion of his considerable dark side power, Kun destroyed the wyrm and earned the Massassi's loyalty. Kun in turn banished Nadd's spirit<ref name="dlots4" /> and discovered Sadow's buried ''Corsair'',<ref name="dlots5" /> using the ship in his own [[Great Sith War/Legends|unsuccessful quest]] for Sith domination of the galaxy.<ref name="nec" /> Kun was not the only future Sith to discover knowledge of Sadow's alchemy. The Dark Lord [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], who lived several thousand years after Sadow's time, found an ancient [[holocron]] containing detailed records of Sadow's work, recorded in the long-dead Dark Lord's voice. Sidious guarded this knowledge tightly, but found himself sorely tempted to include some of Sadow's work in ''[[The Creation of Monsters]]'', the third volume of Sidious' ''[[Dark Side Compendium]]''.<ref name="jvs" />

Although Sadow's fleet was almost completely destroyed in the Great Hyperspace War,<ref name="fotse5" /> the [[Sith dreadnaught]]<ref name="crosscurrent" /> ''Omen''&mdash;which Sadow had sent with Captain Yaru Korsin to mine Lignan crystals at Phaegon III&mdash;miraculously survived a Jedi attack to crash-land on the uncharted planet of [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]].<ref name="precipice" /> There, Korsin and some of his crew survived to conquer the native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] and form a powerful, isolated [[Lost Tribe of Sith]], which after generations dimly remembered Naga Sadow as Korsin's "celestial ally." In [[3000 BBY]], however, a recording of Sadow's original orders sending Korsin to Phaegon III was discovered by Tribe members, causing a major furor.<ref name="pantheon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref> The ''Omen''{{'s}} sister ship, the ''Harbinger'', also survived the disaster at Phaegon III, only to emerge [[41 ABY|almost five thousand years later]] after traveling through an unstable hyperspace tunnel.<ref name="crosscurrent" />

Sadow's personal records fell into the hands of the secret [[Jedi Covenant]] by the time of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], which they used to launch their own pursuit of the Muur Talisman that had evaded Sadow's reach during his lifetime.<ref name="kotor25" /> Some other remnants of Sadow's Sith Empire survived the war as well, [[Sith exodus|chased into deep space]] by the Republic. They followed a new [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]], who reconstituted the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] on the forgotten colony of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] and plotted his own [[Great Galactic War|attempt]] for galactic power.<ref name="timeline12">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War|int=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War}}</ref> Some Jedi, including the respected Jedi Master [[Gnost-Dural]], believed at one point this mysterious Sith Emperor to be none other than Naga Sadow himself, returned from exile.<ref name="gnost">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']]</ref> One agent of the new Sith Empire, [[Darth Zash]], boasted a complete collection of Sadow's writings from Yavin 4.<ref name="zash">{{TORcite|type=|Conversation with Darth Zash}}</ref>

Long after the death of Naga Sadow, treasure hunters scoured the galaxy for a [[Force crystal of Naga Sadow|force crystal]] that presumably belonged to the Sith Lord. Although its existence was debated by the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the explorer [[Riyan Kiner]] became utterly insane after spending his life looking for this fabled artifact.<ref name="SWG:TMHP1">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|The Meatlumps Hideout, Part 1|Corellia}}</ref>

====Sadow's tomb====
{{Quote|To set foot in the tomb of Naga Sadow is to breathe in death itself.|[[Darth Baras]]|<ref name="TFT">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|The Final Trial|Korriban}}</ref>}}
Sometime after Sadow's death, a "[[Tomb of Naga Sadow]]" was built on Korriban, its entrance marked with a large stone relief of Sadow's face,<ref name="shadows">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref> although Sadow's actual remains instead rested in a more modest [[Naga Sadow's tomb|tomb]] on Yavin 4. Sadow's tomb on Korriban, which contained an ancient [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Star Map]] containing directions to the Rakatan [[Star Forge]],<ref name="kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> became a nest of [[terentatek]] beasts that killed Jedi Knights [[Duron Qel-Droma]] and [[Shaela Nuur]] in [[3993 BBY]].<ref name="shadows" /> The Dark Lord of the Sith-turned-Jedi Knight [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] twice entered Sadow's tomb to find the Star Map.<ref name="kotor" /> In [[3951 BBY]],<ref name="nec" /> [[Meetra Surik]] found rocks blocking the tomb's entrance.<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> Although Sadow's Korriban tomb did not contain his remains, Sadow constructed [[Droid/Legends|droid]] sentries to protect its inner chambers, guarding among other things an ancient [[Dashade/Legends|Dashade]] warrior known as [[Khem Val]], who lived in stasis within the crypt's walls for centuries after being placed there by the Sith Lord [[Tulak Hord]]. Around [[3643 BBY]], a [[Darth Nox|Sith acolyte]] managed to breach the tomb and acquire the Star Map, with the help of the freed Khem Val.<ref name="sadowtombquest">{{TORcite|type=general|A Map for the Future|Korriban}}</ref>

Meanwhile, Sadow's actual resting place remained in relative obscurity, protected by the descendants of his Massassi slaves, and there Sadow's spirit continued to linger. During the era of the Great Galactic War, Sadow's tomb on Yavin 4 was discovered by the Jedi Master [[Barel Ovair]] and his apprentice [[Eison Gynt]], who had tracked Sadow's legacy down in an attempt to dispel his spirit. After being attacked by Massassi guards, Ovair left Gynt behind and returned to Republic space, but Gynt survived to be possessed by Sadow. Several years later, Gynt, still under Sadow's thrall, dressed in Massassi garb and returned to Coruscant. Gynt publicly [[Duel on Coruscant (Inter–Sith Wars Period)|attacked]] Ovair upon his return, but Ovair defeated and slew him, neutralizing Sadow's spirit.<ref name="timeline7">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?|int=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?}}</ref> Sadow's spirit was not completely gone, however. During one [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Galactic War)|period of intense Force activity]] on the moon<ref name="shadow of revan">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan]]''</ref> in [[3637 BBY]],<ref name="TOR date">{{TOR_updates|3.0}}</ref> Sadow's spirit manifested as a ghost in the jungles of Yavin 4.<ref name="shadow of revan" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I fight for the future&hellip; and the future is now!|Naga Sadow|<ref name="gaots2" />}}
[[File:Naga_Sadow_WotC.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Sith Lord Naga Sadow]]
A visionary, Naga Sadow was possessed of a driving ambition that led him not only to crave the title of Dark Lord of the Sith, but to dream of piercing the Stygian Caldera and bringing the splendor of the Sith Empire to the entire galaxy.<ref name="paragon" /> More than that, Sadow was a rebel, believing that only he could determine his place in the galaxy, refusing to bow to tradition and daring to fight against what he saw as the Sith Empire's stagnation and complacency. This rebelliousness was fueled by a sense of responsibility he felt to his exile ancestors, whom he recalled as great Jedi who created a flame that Sadow refused to let burn out. As such, he rued what he saw as "backwards thinkers," men like Ludo Kressh, who Sadow believed would lead to the Sith Empire's ruin.<ref name="gaots2" /> Pursuing opportunity wherever it arose, Sadow chafed at the isolationism of the Sith Empire, believing it to be a practical impossibility for such a sprawling body. It was this expansionist philosophy that came to define Sadow long before he ever became Dark Lord, as he became known as an impassioned speaker who consistently preached a new, progressive future for the Sith Empire. Sadow was also remarkably cunning, quick-thinking<ref name="gaots3" /> and tactically inventive;<ref name="gaots5" /> within days of the Daragons' arrival in Sith Space, Sadow had already formulated the plan that would bring him to the cusp of galactic domination,<ref name="gaots3" /> a plot that required him to brilliantly outmaneuver his greatest rival, Ludo Kressh.<ref name="gaots5" />

Sadow stood apart from the Sith establishment in every sense of the term, being one of the few to recognize the problems underlying the glory of the Sith Empire and dedicating his life to fighting them.<ref name="warfare" /> Among the few of the Sith "old guard" that Sadow respected was his teacher Simus, but Sadow did away with his old mentor the minute that it suited him.<ref name="gaots3" /> Despite this, he was still a strong believer that the Sith Empire was superior to all alternatives, especially the "oppressive system" of the Galactic Republic. Sadow often displayed a strong disrespect for any who would oppose him, saving his most venomous invective for his rival Ludo Kressh, who disgusted the Dark Lord with his adherence to tradition and opposition to Sadow's progressive ways.<ref name="fotse1" /> Sadow craved contact with the unknown, and was always searching for chances to expand, dominate and control beyond the borders of the Sith Empire. He lacked the fear of the Republic and the outside galaxy that was common among the Sith of the day&mdash;to him, the Republic and the Jedi were not the hidden monsters that defeated his ancestors, just a new field to conquer.<ref name="gaots3" /> He also held none of the [[Speciesism|xenophobia]] that characterized many of his peers, such as Ludo Kressh. To Sadow, outsiders could be just as Sith as any born in the Empire, and Humans and members of other species often enjoyed high standing with the Dark Lord.<ref name="paragon" />

Sadow's humaneness and even respect for different peoples and cultures stood in stark contrast to his belief that, as a powerful Sith alchemist, the natural order of the universe belonged to him and existed to be twisted to serve Sadow.<ref name="dlots5" /> Even his loyalest servants, the Massassi, existed only to defend him and pay him tribute, and he felt no remorse for twisting them into mindless beasts.<ref name="massassicodex" /> All the destruction he could cause, including the death of a star system, was a small price to pay to further Sadow's aims.<ref name="dlots1" /> Sadow was adept at playing the role of caring host when it suited him,<ref name="gaots4" /> but it only ever lasted as long as it suited his purposes,<ref name="gaots5" /> he was vicious and precise in his strike once given an opening.<ref name="lokar">{{TORcite|type=|Conversation with Lord [[Lokar]]}}</ref> In the end, however, Sadow's overconfidence wound up being his downfall, and he felt shamed by his loss of glory when forced into exile at the end of the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="fotse5" /> Sadow stood 1.88 [[meter]]s tall, and had brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and green [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="negtc" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Here in my meditation chamber I can see the galaxy in my mind's eye&hellip; I can visualize vast armies, powerful fleets, invincible warriors&hellip; and with Sith arts, my imagination can make them real!|Naga Sadow|<ref name="fotse4" />}}
[[File:NagaSadowSupernova-TFotSE5.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Naga Sadow wrenches fire from the stars.]]
A powerful dark magician, Naga Sadow was remembered long after his death as a master of Sith alchemy who had the ability to twist the natural order of the universe to serve his purposes. With his magic, Sadow could transform the living into monstrous, brutal beasts, his own malformed servants of death&mdash;<ref name="dlots5" /> and, it was said, to give flesh to those spirits already departed.<ref name="dlots3" /> Sadow could also focus his gift of alchemy and magic into greater displays of Force power, including causing supernovas<ref name="fotse4" /> and solar flares to cover his retreat at the end of the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="fotse5" /> But Sadow's power in the Force went beyond just the Sith alchemy that he was known, and feared, for. Sadow was incredibly potent at creating illusions, focusing his energy for such pursuits in his Sith meditation sphere. When in his sphere, Sadow had the ability to conjure hundreds of illusions at once and manifest them [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]] away. Sadow's power of illusion was so great that he made it one of the focal points of his plan during the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="fotse3" /> However, Sadow was not able to sustain these illusions when his concentration was even briefly broken, as it was when Gav Daragon turned on him at Primus Goluud.<ref name="fotse4" />

A brilliant strategist, Sadow's strengths lied not in direct confrontation, but in his mastery of the ability to intuit where his foe was weakest and then strike precisely and devastatingly.<ref name="lokar" /> As a Sith Lord, however, Sadow was no stranger to individual combat, and was a match for Ludo Kressh with his favored Force-imbued [[Sith sword]]. Sadow often employed [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]] while in single combat, pausing his sword strikes to pelt his opponent with stones using the Force.<ref name="gaots2" /> Sadow also proved himself handy with a Republic blaster in his breakout of Gav and Jori Daragon from imprisonment on Ziost, even though he had never seen a weapon of its type before and the Sith of the time largely fought with swords and spears.<ref name="gaots5" /> Sadow was fluent in his native [[Sith (language)|Sith]] and the [[Massassi (language)|tongue]] of his Massassi slaves, as well as the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]] of his Jedi ancestors.<ref name="dss" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Here is the power to wrench fire from the stars&hellip;|Exar Kun, discovering the true power of Naga Sadow's ''Corsair''|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:SWOmnibusTOTJ1-art.png|thumb|right|300px|Sadow made use of amulets, crystals and a Sith meditation sphere to augment his power.]]
As one of the most powerful alchemists and Sith sorcerers of all time, much of Sadow's equipment was used to focus and augment his dark talents. Sadow was able to wield his greatest alchemical power on his ''Derriphan''-class battleship, the ''Corsair'',<ref name="kotorcg">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> which had an array of [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] in a platform on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]]. Through these crystals, Sadow was able to summon nigh-unlimited power, including the ability to obliterate stars themselves. Sadow also owned a Sith meditation sphere which served as his center for creating illusions, and he was able to achieve this at an incredibly large scale during the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="fotse4" /> One of Naga Sadow's most striking possessions was the bejeweled Sith amulets that he wore on his hands, which he used to help focus dark side energy for his alchemical pursuits.<ref name="gaots3" />

The left amulet survived to eventually fall into the possession of Exar Kun, via the Massassi priest [[Zythmnr]] on Yavin 4.<ref name="dlots4" /> Years before the use of the lightsaber became common among Sith Lords, Naga Sadow did battle with a Force-imbued [[Sith sword]] with which he became quite proficient.<ref name="dss" /> He also used a [[Naga Sadow's poison blade|poisoned blade]].<ref name="kotor" /> The Sith Lord also had his own suit of body armor, which survived past his death. Sadow's armor was elaborate and gold-plated, with a chest piece featuring a large, red eye and spikes on its [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]].<ref name="armor">{{TORcite|type=|Item: Naga Sadow's Armor Set}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception and development===
{{Quote|But about 5,000 standard years before the Battle of Yavin, the Republic discovered the Sith empire. An ambitious Dark Lord of the Sith named Naga Sadow decided he could conquer the vast Republic and began the Great Hyperspace War. His armies were defeated by the Jedi Knights.|[[Stephen J. Sansweet]]|<ref name="Ask">{{SWArchive|url=community/askjc/steve/askjc20000619.html|text=What exactly is a Sith Lord? What is the history of the Sith? I have not seen anything about this group of people except that they were defeated by the Jedi Order at some point.}}</ref>}}
[[File:SadowSketch.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Naga Sadow concept sketch]]
Naga Sadow first appeared in the opening scene of [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - Dark Lords of the Sith'']], a story arc in the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series, written by [[Tom Veitch]] and [[Kevin J. Anderson]] and released in [[1994]]. Sadow appears in a flashback to the end of his unsuccessful war on the Republic,<ref name="dlots1" /> a story that would later receive its own story arcs, [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith|''Tales of the Jedi: The Golden Age of the Sith'']] and [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire|''Tales of the Jedi: The Fall of the Sith Empire'']], both written by Anderson, where Sadow appears as a main character.<ref name="gaots2" /><ref name="fotse1" /> Sadow was originally illustrated by [[Chris Gossett]] during his initial appearance in ''Dark Lords of the Sith'',<ref name="dlots1" /> and was drawn by [[Dario Carrasco, Jr.]] during his appearances in ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' and ''The Fall of the Sith Empire''.<ref name="gaots2" /><ref name="fotse1" />

===Inconsistencies===
{{Quote|The greatest Sith magicians and priests chafed under the rule of the Jedi Dark lords. There was actually a conflict between the two factions, which resulted in the death of many great Sith and the banishment of the Sith magician Naga Sadow to Yavin Four.|Tom Veitch|<ref name="comicscan">{{GalaxyCite|8|ComicScan|ComicScan: Taken by Force}}</ref>}}
Sadow's early mentions and his appearances in ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' and ''The Fall of the Sith Empire'' contain several inconsistencies between them. Tom Veitch's account of Sadow's backstory presented in ''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' was heavily revised by the ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' comic series written by Kevin J. Anderson: originally, Vodo Bass said that Sadow was a Sith sorcerer and member of an elite priesthood of pure Sith blood who fled to Yavin 4 after being banished from the Sith Empire for rebelling against the ruling Dark Lord, a Dark Jedi who ruled over the Sith people, and being branded a criminal by the Republic.<ref name="dlots1" /> Additionally, [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]] and [[Star Wars Insider 26|''Star Wars Insider'' 26]] place Sadow's defeat and flight to Yavin 4 at 4990 BBY,<ref name="fotse5" /><ref name="insider26">{{InsiderCite|26|The Horse's Mouth|Straight from the Horse's Mouth: A Guide to the ''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'' Universe, Part 1}}</ref> although later sources changed that date to 5000 BBY.<ref name="nec" />

[[File:NagaSadow-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|150px|Naga Sadow with a more Human-like appearance in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'']]
These inconsistencies extended to the circumstances of Sadow's death. Although earlier sources remained ambiguous on Sadow's death,<ref name="tec" /><ref name="secrets2000">''[[Star Wars: Secrets of the Sith]]''</ref><ref name="dss" /><ref name="negtc" /><ref name="FF90">{{FactFile|90|NAD 1-4|The Shadow of Freedon Nadd}}</ref> the Freedon Nadd entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' definitively states that Nadd destroyed Sadow's spirit,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|355|Nadd, Freedon}}</ref> as do most other more recent Legends sources when referring to Naga Sadow's death.<ref name="nec" /><ref name="naddcodex" /><ref name="naddshort">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' Description of [[Freedon Nadd's short lightsaber]]</ref> Before the release of the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', IGN reported that the game's Sith Emperor was Naga Sadow,<ref name="ign">{{WebCite|url=http://pc.ign.com/articles/922/922656p1.html|text=Star Wars: The Old Republic Story Details|author=Steve Butts|date=2008-10-22|archivedate=20081104144150}}</ref> but subsequent sources confirmed that the Sith Emperor was not Sadow, but rather a Sith Lord from his Empire who avoided participation in the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> However, Sadow's spirit still appeared in ''The Old Republic''<ref name="shadow of revan" /> along with other ''Old Republic'' supplementary materials,<ref name="timeline7" /> contradicting the sources saying that Nadd definitively destroyed Sadow. 

[[File:Naga_Sadow-Timeline12.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Naga Sadow, Human/Sith hybrid]]
There are other discrepancies regarding Sadow's physical appearance. Although Sadow's ''The Golden Age of the Sith'' and ''The Fall of the Sith Empire'' appearances consistently portray him as having the reddish skin typical of the Sith species as well as brown eyes,<ref name="gaots2" /><ref name="fotse1" /> Sadow's depiction in ''Dark Lords of the Sith'' and ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'' shows him with a more Human appearance, with lighter skin<ref name="dlots1" /> and green eyes.<ref name="negtc" /> As many other Sadow depictions are truer to his later comic appearance,<ref name="jvs" /><ref name="nec" /> this article treats his later appearance as being correct.
